title: Deachamh a' Chogaidh is proclaimed
summary: Within days of Àth leathan the council lays a tithe of one part in twelve on every sale of dubhan in the kingdom, for the war's sake and, the order says twice, for a time only.

title: A clerk of An t-Ionmhas is sent to Muileann òg
summary: Cailean Ros of An t-Ionmhas comes to sit beside the fair pump at Muileann òg and mark the tithe on every gallon drawn; Ùna nic Ailein shows him the tank's own measure, which nobody in the capital had thought to teach him.

title: The first tithe taken at Muileann òg
summary: Ùna nic Ailein records the first gallon of dubhan sold under Deachamh a' Chogaidh at the Muileann òg pump, eleven gallons to Seumas Buidhe the smith, one part in twelve set aside before the coin changes hands.

title: The first complaint against the tithe
summary: In the fifth week of the tithe, Barabal nic Rath, a weaver of Muileann òg, brings her own five weeks' reckoning of it to Cùirt na Fèille and asks that her complaint against its silence on its own ending be written into the book.

title: An seachdamh rèisimeid raised
summary: News of An seachdamh rèisimeid, raised on the west coast to hold the road behind the army, reaches Muileann òg and Caol mhòr weeks after the fact, carried by carters rather than any order.

title: A' chiad rèisimeid raised at Inis mhòr
summary: A' chiad rèisimeid is raised at Inis mhòr from the capital's own companies, to stand about the council, the mint and the bridge over the Abhainn dhomhain; word of it is old before it reaches the north.

title: A' chiad chabhlach raised at Àth gharbh
summary: A' chiad chabhlach is raised from the south-west harbours and stationed at Àth gharbh, its hulls lying at Doire shean, and sent round the western cape to close the Tuathaich coast to trade.

title: An ceathramh cabhlach raised at Cuan shean
summary: An ceathramh cabhlach is raised at Cuan shean and joins the first off the Tuathaich coast. Together the two close the sea-reach of the western Seann Skell and of Cnoc bhàn in the north-west to every hull but the fishing boats, and search those.

title: An ceathramh cabhlach searches the boats at Caol mhòr
summary: A hull of An ceathramh cabhlach boards and searches every boat at Caol mhòr's harbour wall for dubhan or coal carried against the closing of the coast; the engine-boats Joe Ashby has fitted are searched last and longest.

title: Joe Ashby is asked to mend a fleet hull
summary: An unsigned letter from Caol mhòr's harbour depot asks Joe Ashby to mend an engine of An ceathramh cabhlach that the depot's own men cannot; the letter is signed with a mark, and names no fleet and no rank.

title: Joe Ashby refits the fleet hull
summary: Joe Ashby and Ned Fowler find and mend a wrongly seated valve aboard an unnamed hull of An ceathramh cabhlach at Caol mhòr's depot jetty, and are paid at the harbour's own rate, in coin, and asked no questions.

title: One part in twelve
summary: Deachamh a' Chogaidh is laid at one part in twelve of every sale of dubhan, taken at the point of sale by a clerk of An t-Ionmhas sitting beside the pump.

title: Cailean Ros given the cold corner
summary: An t-Ionmhas's young clerk at the Muileann òg pump, Cailean Ros, is given the coldest corner of the toll-house's upper room against the weather, and takes it without complaint.

title: The lieutenant laughs at Will Tanner's locker
summary: Searching the boats at Caol mhòr, An ceathramh cabhlach's lieutenant finds Will Tanner's false locker under the stern thwart with nothing in it but a jar of spirit, laughs once, and writes nothing of it.

title: The depot's tally names no fitter
summary: The fleet depot at Caol mhòr enters the mending of a hull's engine and the sum paid out, and names no fitter.

title: The tithe-clerks' first returns
summary: An t-Ionmhas's clerks at the pumps send in their first month's returns; the clerk at Muileann òg's is the neatest and the smallest.

title: Hay cleared from the barracks at Inis mhòr
summary: The farmers of Seann Vell are given a week to take their hay out of the barracks at Inis mhòr when A' chiad rèisimeid is raised there; what is not taken is fed to the regiment's horses.

title: The ferrymen of Àth gharbh go to A' chiad chabhlach
summary: Four of the ferrymen of Àth gharbh go into A' chiad chabhlach at its raising, and the ferry at the walled ford is worked through the war by the oldest of them and his daughter.

title: The chandlers of Cuan shean
summary: The chandlers of Cuan shean, An ceathramh cabhlach's harbour, sell out of rope and canvas within a month of the fleet's raising and send to Ros dhomhain for more at a price they say is war.

title: A tithe-clerk at the pans of Caol ìseal
summary: An t-Ionmhas's clerk for the tithe sits at the dubhan pump by the salt pans of Caol ìseal; the salt-boilers pay their part in twelve on every barrel for the pans and grumble that salt pays twice.
